text:
ana: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector roll we see a ~10-15% perf regression on 2-token tail steps for a few customers. Traces point at KV cache memcpy hotpaths. Has anyone chased alignment/stride interactions recently?

ben: Which model/hardware/dtype/workload? quick context helps.

ana: model: redwood-7B-v1 (fp16), infra: A100-40GB, workload: batch=1, avg seq=512 -> regression shows up on the final generate step (2-token tails). Root cause looks like heavy memcpy/uncached loads during KV read. :confused:

perf-bot: profile summary (top stacks):
```
memcpy                                                                 42.3%
kv_read_unaligned_loads                                              26.8%
flash_attn_fused_kernel                                               18.5%
other                                                                  12.4%
```
flame: /artifacts/1792345678/flame.html

cheng: My hunch: kernel-selector switched to a fused-flash variant that assumes per-head contiguous KV (separate layout) and 32B vector alignment. Our allocator currently gives 16B alignment for fp16 when packed; interleaved layout + 16B stride -> uncoalesced loads, hence memcpy fallback. Did the selector change priority recently?

evan: Yeah we defaulted to prefer fused kernels for lower-latency profiles. Also pushed a dtype-default tweak to prefer bf16 kernels if available (might change packing). Could be interplay between dtype packing and head stride. :thinking:

ben: Quick experiment we can run: force layout=separate and force alignment=64 and re-run perf to isolate. E.g.:
```
export RW_KV_LAYOUT=separate
export RW_KV_MIN_ALIGN=64
./bin/serve-bench --model redwood-7B-v1 --dtype fp16 --batch 1 --seq 512 --tokens 10000
```
If throughput recovers, we know it's alignment/stride.

ana: Ran that locally on a repro box. Results: separate+align64 -> throughput +12%, p99 token latency down ~18%. Baseline (interleaved/align16) = 400 toks/s, separate+align64 = 448 toks/s. Memory overhead +~2% due to padding. Logs: /artifacts/1792345678/bench.log

cheng: Good signal. That matches the uncoalesced load theory. We need to decide: change allocator to guarantee 64B for KV buffers, or make kernel selector always check detected layout/stride and avoid fused kernel when layout is interleaved/unaligned.

evan: Two implementation paths:
- cheap: kernel selector heuristic that checks (layout, dtype, head_size, alignment) before choosing fused.
- robust: allocator fix to provide 64B alignment for KV (affects memory, may add padding).
Which do we prefer for fast remediation?

ben: For immediate fix, add selector guard + a quick rollback flag in rollout. Longer term, allocator change + tests. Also add a microbench that tests kernels across layouts during CI.

ana: I'll open a triage PR today that: 1) adds a selector check (if layout==interleaved && head_size % 32 != 0 -> avoid fused), 2) adds env override RW_KV_LAYOUT for customers, 3) documents the memory tradeoff.

cheng: Also add a small instrumentation point: record kv_buffer_alignment and kv_stride in per-request trace so perf-bot can auto-detect regressions tied to alignment.

perf-bot: noted: will add an alert rule: if median tokens/s drops >5% vs baseline and kv_stride/alignment differs from baseline -> create incident draft.

evan: Can we also check dtype fallback? If bf16 vs fp16 packing changes we might hit the same issue. Selector should include dtype check.

ana: Yes — PR will include dtype guard. Quick follow-up: can someone run the separate+align64 test on gcp-pool-2 (customer repro) and post numbers? I can patch rollout once we confirm.

ben: I'll run it now and post results in ~20m.

deploy-bot: rollout:kernel-selector:v2 -> PAUSED (manual pause by canary after perf alert).

ana: Thanks all — summary: likely root cause = fused kernel chosen when KV layout/stride/alignment incompatible -> uncoalesced accesses + memcpy regressions. Short-term: selector guard + rollout pause. Long-term: allocator alignment or layout-agnostic kernels.

cheng: I'll draft a small benchmark harness for head-stride/alignment corners and add to eng-runtime perf tests.

ana: Perfect. Will file follow-ups in GH and link here. :thumbsup:
